subject: Design review: split-operator delegation & verifiable key ceremony for NexusCloud private deploy
messages:
From: Nexus Cloud Onboarding <onboard@nexuscloud.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: key custody model and operator delegation for Nexus private VPC deployment

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today. Nexus is moving toward a staged private deployment in our EU/US regions and the security team asked us to formalize how BYOK/HSM custody will work when we operate fully air-gapped operator nodes. Two asks to kick off the doc: 

1) Can Redwood propose a split-operator delegation pattern (minimal live keys on site, operator unseal with multi-person control) with concrete steps we can audit?
2) We need a verifiable evidence package for our auditors: what logs/attestations will Redwood produce at ceremony time?

I've attached a short Nexus draft (nexus-split-ceremony-proposal.pdf) that sketches our constraints (no external egress during ceremony, two-person presence, ACME witness allowed).

If possible, can we have a short internal proposed procedure + an example access matrix by Friday? Our compliance lead (Acme Industrial Security) is copied.

Cheers,
Nora Chang
Nexus Cloud Onboarding
Attachment: nexus-split-ceremony-proposal.pdf (application/pdf)

---

Note: please treat this as onboarding-equivalent pre-production info.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Nexus Cloud Onboarding <onboard@nexuscloud.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: key custody model and operator delegation for Nexus private VPC deployment

Nora / Acme team —

Thanks for the clear brief and the constraints doc. High level we recommend a 3-stage, auditable split-operator ceremony that meets air-gap requirements and provides verifiable artefacts:

- Pre-ceremony: sealed artifacts staged on encrypted USB (signed manifests), roles enumerated (Operator A, Operator B, Auditor/Witness), and a dedicated ephemeral KMS wrapping key created by Redwood’s control plane and exported via an HSM-protected wrapping key share.
- Ceremony (on‑site, air‑gapped): dual-control unseal using threshold shares (2-of-3), ephemeral wrapping performed inside customer HSM, immediate locally-stored immutable audit bundle (signed hash chain + timestamped attestation) written to two independent drives. No outbound network egress permitted.
- Post-ceremony: evidence ingestion: the signed hash and attestations are uploaded to a mutually agreed S3 bucket (or exchanged on hardened media) and Redwood posts a verifiable statement to our audit API (read-only) with signed metadata and the ceremony certificate ID.

Concrete deliverables we can provide:
- Operator access matrix (see attached) with role definitions and step-by-step operator actions.
- Draft ceremony script (time-boxed steps, witness checklist).
- Audit bundle format spec and sample signed attestation.

Two immediate questions for Nexus:
1) Do you require an HSM vendor preference (e.g., Thales vs. Utimaco) or will Nexus provide hardware?
2) Does Acme want to act purely as witness, or do you require access to a read-only copy of the audit bundle immediately after ceremony?

I'll attach the operator access matrix and a short ceremony script for review. If this looks OK, Vanessa and Mina will join the live rehearsal planning.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachment: operator-access-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Nexus Cloud Onboarding <onboard@nexuscloud.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: key custody model and operator delegation for Nexus private VPC deployment

Nora / team — quick operational notes from infra before the rehearsal planning: 

- Network/NICs: confirm that the ceremony host VM will have no upstream default gateway and that ARP/ICMP is restricted to the local switch. We'll provide a checklist for NIC isolation.
- USB hygiene: we require vendor-signed Yubikey/USB keys for signing manifests; any third-party media must be hashed and verified prior to use.
- Time sync: if the site is truly air-gapped we will include an internal GPS/secure-time appliance in the checklist; otherwise rely on hardware RTC with attestation.
- Operator tokens: tokens used to split the HSM wrap key will be generated from an HSM-backed RNG on the Redwood side and delivered as sealed shares. For ceremony recovery, an 'escrow recovery' process exists but requires executive sign-off and multi-party approval (outlined in the attached DocuSign agreement).

Action items:
- Nexus: confirm HSM vendor or supply order number.
- Acme: confirm whether the auditor will require an immediate copy of the audit bundle or delayed transfer.
- Redwood: we will prepare the rehearsal script and a red-team checklist for the rehearsal (no real keys).

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Private Deploy Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Acme Industrial Security <security@acmeindustrial.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Nexus Cloud Onboarding <onboard@nexuscloud.io>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2026 23:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: key custody model and operator delegation for Nexus private VPC deployment

Jonas / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turn. Acme reviewed the proposal and the following clarifications are required before we sign off for production ceremony: 

1) Chain of custody form: we require pre-stamped, signed chain-of-custody PDF for all physical drives used to store the audit bundle; this must include serials and operator IDs.
2) Attestation verification: Redwood must publish a small verification CLI (or a documented verification recipe) so auditors can independently validate the signed audit bundle without Redwood’s control plane.
3) Escrow recovery gating: the executive sign-off flow must include a human-readable checklist and a replayable audit trail. We will not accept opaque automated recovery.

If Redwood can provide a sample chain-of-custody template and the verifier docs by Tuesday, Acme will be able to approve a rehearsal next week. We are prepared to witness the rehearsal remotely (video feed) or in-person depending on Nexus scheduling.

Regards,
D. Patel
Lead, Security Assurance | Acme Industrial Security
Attachment: docsign-key-escrow-agreement.pdf (application/pdf)
